reader.requirement: At --std 85 two nonnumeric operands (elementary alphanumeric, alphabetic, edited, group, literal, figurative, or a numeric integer imaged per sublist 1) of equal size compare character by character from the high-order end, the first unequal pair deciding by its position in the program collating sequence (native unless OBJECT-COMPUTER names one), and are equal when every pair is equal.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel < 2002: the numeric operand of a character comparison is imaged by OperandText.AsItemCharacters (the §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 sublist-1 temporary of the item's own size) instead of OperandText.AsString; it shapes the operand image only, the character-by-character comparison and padding after it are the same CobolString.Compare/CobolCollation call
DialectLevel < 2002 with a group operand: a signed numeric item keeps its separate sign character opposite a 1985 group (sublist-1 item 2); again the operand image, not the comparison rule

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|IsAtLeast|Dialect|Constructs.|Std' over ConditionRenderer.cs, ConditionBinder.cs, CollatingModel.cs, StatementValidation.cs; 'Dialect|Edition|Version' over CobolCollation.cs, CobolString.cs, CobolVarGroup.cs (no hit in the runtime). The two ConditionRenderer hits above are the only switches on the alphanumeric-comparison path; ConditionBinder's Edition.Has(2002) (line 941) governs negated abbreviated relations, not this rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: for THIS rule the comparison is the same CobolString.Compare/CobolCollation call at every edition; the 1985 arms of ComparisonText/DropsOperationalSign change only how a numeric operand is imaged before it (sublist 1), and the probes print the same at --std 85 and --std 2023

reader.notes: Alphanumeric relations render CobolString.Compare (native ordinal, high-order first) or, under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, the CobolCollation table chosen by CollateArgFor over both operands' categories. Every probe printed the text's result, identically at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-020/r1.cob, r2.cob at --std 85. 1985-only arms: ZZ9 '  5' = 5 F and < 5 T (the literal imaged as '5', size 1, a 1985 nonnumeric comparison); S999 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -12 vs X(4) '012 ' T (sign not moved) but vs a group '-012' T (group move keeps the sign), identical output at 2023 differs (8 F), so the 1985 arm is real and right; 99PP 1200 vs '12' T, vs '1200' F (temp sized 2, P not counted in the size, per §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 GR1 'same size as the numeric data item'). Collating: ALPHABET Y IS 'B' 'A' ALSO 'a' 'D' THROUGH 'F' ' ' as PCS: 'A' = 'a' T and neither < nor > (ALSO same ordinal, cite.py OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4d 'assigned to the same ordinal position in the collating sequence'); E > A T; E < C (unlisted) T; B = LOW-VALUE T; MOVE LOW-VALUE gives 'BB'; numeric 1 > 'A' T. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 GRL2.1. Side note, not this rule: COBOL3146 cites §2023:8.8.4.2.1 at --std 85.
